commits.message: A derived palette's foreground-muted reads stronger than its foreground-disabled, on every bundled base (rich-unfiled-791c.tofk)

De-emphasized widget text is drawn in foreground-muted, held to its 3:1 floor, not terminal dim (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs) (#586)

* De-emphasized widget text is drawn in foreground-muted, held to its 3:1 floor, not terminal dim (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

* Widget contrast is a setting, and sixteen colors draw the theme's own (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

A themed widget takes `contrast`, the TextFit its text meets a floor with:
slide by default, TEXT_FITS.asIs to turn checking off, setContrast to change
it live. Widgets resolve colors at the frame's depth through one
ThemedWidget.ink; at an indexed depth a pair is written in the theme's own
sixteen rather than rounded against stock VGA, and muted text is the slot
each theme states (ThemePaletteData.ansiMuted, TerminalTheme.mutedSlot), so
a placeholder no longer looks typed at 16 colors. mutedInk owns the muted
look; a disabled TextInput's continuation marker is drawn disabled. The
contrast test names muted glyphs by scene, not by color.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Widget ink reads the frame's terminal, holds a stated muted slot to its floor (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

Medium review of 1c30a79ba. At an indexed depth a widget's pair is chosen
among the colors RenderOptions.terminal shows (resolveTerminal, as Effect
and ProgressBar do), and the muted slot is that terminal's: mutedSlot moves
to TerminalColors, validated 0-15, and a terminal whose sixteen are all its
foreground is refused. Grounds are never written as the default. The stated
slot is muted text's candidate at sixteen colors only, held to the floor and
handed to the fit on a miss. Receding from body text belongs to the intent
(recedesFrom in text-on.ts), so text-muted has it too. Slot OKLab is taken
once per terminal and depth.

BREAKING: WidgetBase.ground and ThemedWidget.disabledInk are functions of
the frame's drawing (colorSystem, terminal), not getters; a subclass
overriding either takes the argument.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Widget ink at indexed depths: grey grounds stay grey, muted recedes or dims (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

Extra-high review of c048ae96b. terminal-contrast now runs every scene at
sixteen and 256 colors, with no terminal named and on the theme's own, and
caught each defect before the fix. A ground is the indexed slot that stands
for it, scored by deltaE_OK plus a cost for chroma it lacks, so a dark grey
never becomes VGA maroon or navy, and it is never written as the default.
No text is written in its ground's color. Muted text recedes: a slot other
than the default and its body text's, with less contrast than body text;
where none recedes and reads, it is body text with SGR dim. The fit's tint is
the intent's (textTint). The monochrome refusal leaves TerminalColors. Where
no slot reads, text is the most legible slot. Sorts are min-scans but for
the shades a fit reads on a miss; ground is hoisted out of the line map.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* One contrast engine: writeText in text-on.ts writes a pair at every depth (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

textOn's floor, fit, recede, hue-cost ground, never-on-its-ground and dim
fallback are one function, writeText, which returns the written pair
(ColorSpec text and ground, plus dim). textOn is it read in RGBA, as the
terminal shows the text's slot. widgets/ink.ts is a memoised caller and
slotted is gone from it. The template textOn returns the written color's
name, so at sixteen colors a template writes the slot a widget does.
DrawnAt.terminal widens to TerminalColors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* One rounding rule: roundingDistance in core ranks every slot, writeText rounds by it (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

High review of a4045b654. ColorTable.match, matchReadable, matchWhere,
ColorSpec.matchOn and matchMove rank by roundingDistance: RGB distance plus
a cost for HSV chroma an entry has past slack and twice the value's own, so
a grey stays grey while a dull green may round to a teal. writeText rounds
its ground and candidates by it and its private nearest is gone; at 256
colors it rounds into the writer's table (16-255). readsOn on textOn's
color holds the floor again, tested on every bundled theme at sixteen and
256 colors. The default foreground is a candidate only when a terminal is
named. The template textOn returns the hex of the slot shown, which
composes and rounds back to that slot. A truecolor ground is written drawn
on the palette background. writeText is memoised once and ink's cache is
gone. The terminal-contrast hue check is per cell: a grey ground stays grey.

Review: a CSI and an escape are two lexeme types each read by its own total function, and the no-byte-drawn gate surrounds each sequence with text no final can be (rich-control-codes-xh4n.7c0)
Review: one intermediate range, one count reader, a CSI with a parameter after an intermediate is undrawn, and the text scan owns its cursor (rich-control-codes-xh4n.7c0)

decodeAnsi reads each escape's meaning off the lexer's one parse, so the CSI and escape grammar is defined once (rich-control-codes-xh4n.7c0)

A sequence lexeme carries its introducer kind, parameters, intermediates and
final byte, and sequenceToken dispatches on those fields; ESCAPES' CSI and
escape alternatives and SEQUENCE_BREAK are gone, and the text regex keeps only
what text does. The lexer reads ground text, collected bytes and string
payloads in sticky runs, and drawLine builds its text regex once per line with
no generator per lexeme.

Bench (/tmp/probe590/bench.ts, interleaved min of 15, vs master at 0.30.0):
SGR decode 376 vs 416 ms, scan 234 vs 272; plain decode 266 vs 365, scan 66 vs 182.
